excerpt: Make changes remotely: Easily toggle individual features on and off, and make changes without deploying new code
Just wrap a section of code with a flag, and then use Flagsmith to toggle that feature on or off for different environments, users or user segments.
Target features to users with specific traits (such as geography, subscription level, device type, or application version).
Gradually enable a feature for a percentage of users, either globally or within a segment.
Override feature flags for individual users ("identities"). Enables internal testing, QA, customer support, or personalised experiences at the user level.
Multivariate flags let you define multiple variants with percentage weightings (A/B/n).
Scheduled flags allow you to queue and automatically apply changes to feature flags at a specified future time, eliminating the need for manual intervention at the exact moment of change.
Define stages that your flags progress through automatically, with triggers and actions that control rollouts to selected environments and audiences.
serve variations of a feature with a multivariate flag, collect events from your application into a managed data warehouse, and read the results with a built-in Bayesian statistics engine.

Every action taken within the Flagsmith administration application is tracked and logged. This allows you to easily retrace the events and values that flags, identities and segments have taken over time.
You can stream your Audit Logs into your own infrastructure using Audit Log Webhooks.
Feature Change Requests help creating a four-eyes workflow (create, approve, publish) to updating feature flags, similarly to Pull Requests in GitHub.
Role-based access control (RBAC) provides fine-grained access management of Flagsmith resources.
Self-hosting Flagsmith allows you to run the complete Flagsmith platform within your own infrastructure, giving you full control over your data, security policies, and deployment environment.
You can use Docker to set up an entire Flagsmith Feature Flag environment locally
The Flagsmith Edge Proxy is a service that you host yourself, that allows you to run an instance of the Flagsmith Engine close to your servers.
Authentication: Uses a public, non-secret Environment Key. Security: Open by design. The Environment Key can be exposed in client-side code.
Purpose: Creating, updating, and deleting projects, environments, flags, segments, and users.
The Flagsmith MCP Server gives AI assistants and agents programmatic access to the Flagsmith Admin API through the Model Context Protocol
The Flagsmith CLI lets you manage flags, segments, features, projects and environments from your terminal, and evaluate flags the way an SDK would.
